concept: A 'why it happened' follow-up to this afternoon's '209 to defend' post, so the two read as a pair on the grid. The hero greys out the doubt from earlier (209 didn't look enough) and answers it in bright white (India defended it, series won 3-1). Slide 2 isolates the moment the chase died: 131/6 after 35 overs, with the live-tracker 64% as the twist. Slide 3 turns the scorecard into a wicket bar chart, with Arshdeep's 3/30 lit up as the lead, to show six bowlers shared the job. Slide 4 walks through the last four wickets and asks fans to pick a hero. Cricket blue tag, type and data only: no player photos, no logos.
caption:
209 was enough. Series won 3-1.

This afternoon we asked if 209 could win India the series. It did. New Zealand were bowled out for 187 in 48.1 overs and India won the decider at Bay Oval by 22 runs.

The squeeze: New Zealand were 131/6 after 35 overs, needing 79 from the last 15. Naman Dhir removed Santner, Arshdeep got Clarke, and Axar Patel took the last two.

Arshdeep led the attack with 3/30. Siraj and Axar took two each, and debutant Yash Thakur picked up his first ODI wicket.

Arshdeep or Axar: who won India the decider? Tell us below.
